facts.fact: The World Bank appraisal document of 15 June 2021 states that Gabon's civil registry, which holds birth records, is entirely paper-based in its current form, so no digital link can be built between it and other ID systems.

The World Bank appraisal document of 15 June 2021 describes the civil registry as entirely paper-based and says children are still registered using the legacy paper-based systems; it describes no digital registration of births or deaths.

The World Bank results framework of June 2021 sets the baseline for administrative departments with at least one civil registration office digitally registering vital acts at 0, against targets rising to 5, 10 and 15 in the later years of the project; the indicator counts departments, not offices, and no total is given.
facts.system: Digitalized civil registration system (Digital Gabon sub-component 2.2)

facts.fact: The World Bank appraisal document allots an indicative US$10.5 million of the US$68.5 million IBRD loan to sub-component 2.2, digitalisation of the civil registration system including birth registration; it names no domestic budget line.
facts.system: Digitalized civil registration system (Digital Gabon sub-component 2.2)

facts.fact: The World Bank appraisal document of June 2021 names the Centre national de l'État civil (CNEC), a state entity then being created, as the body that will manage both the NIP and the civil registration systems, and says its institutional mandate still needed clarifying.
facts.system: Digitalized civil registration system (Digital Gabon sub-component 2.2)

systems.owner: CNEC (planned); Digital Gabon project implementation unit
systems.tiers: planned in 2021: a fully digitalised system to register, manage and archive vital records, with a centralised CR database and modules; the results indicator defines digital registration as a fully digitalised process ending with the birth record stored in the centralised database
entirely paper-based in 2021; over 90 per cent of new births registered (DHS 2012); obtaining a birth certificate can require travelling to one's birthplace

systems.platform: to include enrolment, deduplication, NIP issuance and credential production modules
systems.tiers: planned; seed data from legacy voter records, expanded by mass enrolment campaigns
the CNEC is described as its logical continuation
biometric reform of 2011 ended in 2014 in a contract dispute; government locked out of the system since 2014
planned: civil registration and RBPP to interoperate, including issuing the NIP as part of birth registration

note: The legal framework for digitalised civil registration was not in place in June 2021 (baseline No): a draft civil registration law was before government and not yet voted.
